issues.fix: Replace "Lock it before you swing." with "Point your toes down and lock your ankle before you swing." Replace "From about ten metres, drive ten balls under it." with "From ten big steps away, hit ten shots under it. Start at half power. Count how many stay under. No wall? Tie a rope across a goal at knee height."

issues.problem: Club kids say "near post", not "near side". The visual already shows Chalk at the near post.
issues.fix: Replace "He builds a wall and guards the near side." with "He builds a wall and guards the near post."

issues.problem: "On the outside half" does not say outside of what. A kid cannot do this cue at practice. It is the main contact cue for the curler.
issues.fix: Replace "Wipe across the back, like a windscreen wiper, on the outside half." with "Hit just right of centre and wipe across the back, like a windscreen wiper. Left-footed? Flip it."

issues.problem: "Squashy gear" is an odd image for a teen. Few 12-year-olds picture a gear against a rack.
issues.fix: Replace "The ball wraps around your foot and grips, like a squashy gear." with "The ball wraps around your foot and grips, like a tyre on a road." Swap the gear inset for a tyre rolling on a moving road.

issues.problem: Two metaphors name the same air in one breath ("crowd" and "coat"). In "the crowd shoves it the other", "it" can mean the trail or the ball. This is the hardest idea in the video, and the wording makes it harder.
issues.fix: Replace the narration up to "shoves it the other." with: "Air rushes past the ball like a crowd. The spin carries a thin layer of air with it. On one side, that layer moves with the crowd, so the air hugs the ball. On the other side, it fights the crowd, so the air leaves early. <short pause> So the ball throws air to one side, and gets pushed to the other."

issues.problem: Boring stretch: s09 to s11 is about 60 s of X-ray and diagrams with no Tavi, no Chalk and no shot. An impatient kid clicks away here. The last line of s10 also gives a number with no reason to care.
issues.fix: Add a 2 s cutaway of Chalk squinting at the arrows on the last line. Replace "That shove is about half the ball's weight." with "That shove is only about half the ball's weight. But it never stops pushing." This also explains why the gap grows in s11.

issues.problem: "They don't." followed by "grows faster and faster" sounds like a contradiction. To a kid, faster and faster IS bending late. It is the core idea of the chapter.
issues.fix: Replace "Curlers seem to bend late. They don't. <short pause> The gap from a straight line just grows faster and faster." with "Curlers seem to bend late. They don't. They bend the same amount the whole way. <short pause> But the gap from a straight line grows faster and faster."

issues.problem: "Drift" is not a kid word here. "From twenty metres, almost three metres" has no noun, so it is unclear what is three metres. "So the keeper sees it late" gives no reason.
issues.fix: Replace "Twice the distance, four times the drift. From twenty metres, almost three metres. More than the goal is tall." with "Twice the distance, four times the bend. From twenty metres out, it bends almost three metres. That's taller than the goal." Replace "So the keeper sees it late." with "Most of that bend happens in the second half. So the keeper sees it late."

issues.problem: The frisbee icon that slides out of Chalk's mitten has no setup. A kid will not get the joke.
issues.fix: Cut the frisbee icon. Keep the 10% eye grow, which reads on its own.

issues.problem: Coach: "about three metres outside" is true only for a 20 m curler with strong spin. From 10 m the bend is about a quarter of that. A kid who aims 3 m wide at practice misses wide every time.
issues.fix: Replace "So aim about three metres outside your target, and point your standing foot there." with "So aim outside your target, and point your standing foot there. From twenty metres, that's about three metres. Closer in, aim less."

issues.problem: The drill is vague. It does not say where the cone goes, what the target is, or how many kicks to do.
issues.fix: Replace "Solo drill: curl balls around a tall cone into a target." with "Solo drill: put a tall cone halfway to the goal, on the straight line. Curl ten balls around it and in."

issues.problem: The stat sentence is 20 words and has a clause in the middle ("penalties aside"). Heard once, it is hard to follow. The source caption already says "not counting penalties".
issues.fix: Replace "Worth learning: at recent World Cups and Euros, about one goal in five, penalties aside, was a volley or half-volley." with "Worth learning. At recent World Cups and Euros, about one goal in five was a volley or half-volley."

issues.problem: "But" joins two ideas that do not contrast. The "so what" is missing, and so is where the standing foot goes.
issues.fix: Replace the narration with: "Your leg's final whip is faster than a blink. Even so, the ball falls more than its own width. You can't wait for it. <short pause> So set your standing foot early, next to where the ball will drop. Start the swing while the ball is still above your knee."

issues.problem: False claim: from the edge of the box, the goal is about 25 degrees wide. A fist at arm's length covers about 10 degrees, so it covers the height only. A kid who tries this at practice sees goal on both sides of the fist. The line also never says why the fist matters.
issues.fix: Replace "From the edge of the box, the whole goal hides behind it." with "From the edge of the box, your fist covers the goal from grass to bar. That's how small your target is."

issues.problem: "Lean back: the face tilts up." stops before the result, so the kid does not hear the cost.
issues.fix: Replace "Lean back: the face tilts up." with "Lean back: the face tilts up, and the ball climbs over the bar."

issues.problem: "Rolls forward over the top" sounds like the ball rolls over your foot. The cause of the spin is not clear.
issues.fix: Replace "The falling ball slides down your laces, grips, and rolls forward over the top." with "The falling ball rubs against your laces on the way down. That rub spins it forward."

issues.problem: "Harder means higher" is true only at the same launch angle. The video ends on "Low. Hard. In.", so a kid hears that hard is bad and then that hard is good. The line also explains before it shows, which breaks the show-then-explain pattern.
issues.fix: Show SMASH sail over the bar first. Then narrate: "Biggest mistake? Smashing it. <short pause> Same angle, but the harder shot flies over. It arrives sooner, so gravity has less time to pull it down. <short pause> Fix: nose over knee, knee over ball, hit the top half. Clean beats hard."

issues.problem: Safety: a volley at a wall from 2-3 m comes straight back at the face, and the spoken line gives no power limit. "Near a wall" does not say how near. The soap-bubble image does not say why the top of the bounce is the best moment.
issues.fix: Replace "Solo drill: drop the ball near a wall. Volley it at the top of the bounce, where it hangs like a soap bubble." with "Solo drill: stand three big steps from a wall and drop the ball. Hit it at the top of the bounce. There, it hangs almost still, like a soap bubble. Start soft."

issues.problem: "Sits down" is coach slang. The beat gives a fact with no use. The fact itself gives a real tip: a chip loses most of its speed when it lands, so a chip that lands short can stop short.
issues.fix: Replace "When it lands, the chip sits down. The volley runs on." with "When it lands, the chip loses most of its speed. The volley keeps rolling. So land your chip inside the goal."

issues.problem: The cold-open shot was a hard laces drive at 76 km/h that went high. A club kid will say "that wasn't a chip, I blasted it". The spin was chip spin, but the kick was not a chip.
issues.fix: Replace "A chip. Chest behind the ball, foot underneath. Backward spin, by accident." with "It had chip spin. Chest behind the ball, foot underneath. Backward spin, by accident, so it floated over the bar."

issues.problem: "Toes locked" is a new cue. Earlier cues were "toes down, ankle locked". The list also drops the standing-foot fix, which was the direct cure for the car-park miss.
issues.fix: Replace "Knee over the ball. Toes locked. Through the middle." with "Standing foot next to the ball. Knee over it. Toes down, ankle locked."

issues.problem: "Slow turn: speed" puzzles a kid. The drive's line also rolled backward in s06, so "Backward: float" looks like the same spin. The list has four items, but the title says "Three Spins".
issues.fix: Replace "Slow turn: speed. Sideways: bend. Forward: dive. Backward: float." with "Barely turning: fast and straight. Sideways: bend. Forward: dive. Fast backward: float." That leaves three real spins, which matches the title.

issues.problem: "Doesn't turn at all" clashes with "less than once" a second two lines later. A smart kid catches it.
issues.fix: Replace "What if the line doesn't turn at all?" with "What if the line hardly turns?"

issues.problem: The knuckleball teaser works up to "Neither do you." Then "Try it at fifteen or sixteen." gives no reason. To a 12-year-old it sounds like "not for you", so the ending falls flat. Tavi is 14, so an age ticker that starts at 12 is also odd.
issues.fix: Replace "Try it at fifteen or sixteen." with "It needs a hard, dead-centre strike. Nail your drive first. Then try it at fifteen or sixteen." Start the age ticker at 14.

storyboard.title: Three Spins and a Line
storyboard.logline: Alone on a floodlit pitch at nine at night, a young player misses a shot against a goalkeeper they imagined out of chalk. One line drawn on the ball shows the spin behind every fix: a slow backward roll for the laces drive, sideways for the curler, forward for the volley, backward for the chip, and almost none for a knuckleball teaser. Each chapter ends with body cues, the classic mistake and a solo drill for the next practice.

characters.name: Tavi (the player, spoken to only as 'you')
characters.design: Right-footed 14-year-old, about 5.5 heads tall, built only from rounded rectangles and circles (corner radius at least 15% of the short side, no outlines). Teal shirt #3FE0D0 with darker teal shade shapes and one orange chest band #FF7A3D that rhymes with the line on the ball. Shorts #232B5C, teal socks, chalk-white boots #F4F1E8 with a pale lace zone. Warm brown skin #A0673F with one shade #7E4E2F. Rounded cloud-tuft hair in #232B5C. Two oval eyes #151A3D and a small mouth dash. Eyes grow 10% for surprise. Rig: 2-bone IK arms and legs, pelvis turn, spine lean. Idle breathing loop 2-4 px, 3 s. Keyed poses: idle, walk, drop_ball, draw_line, approach, plant, backswing, whip, contact_drive, follow_through, lean_back, curl_wipe, thigh_lift, volley_set, volley_contact, chip_stab, knuckle_stab, shout, fist_out, shrug, pick_up_walk. An age prop (14-16) scales height for the teaser gag.
characters.role: The viewer's stand-in. The narrator never says the name. Tavi misses the first shot, solves one problem per chapter, shows every mistake, fix and drill, and replays the first shot correctly at the end.

characters.name: Chalk (the imagined goalkeeper)
characters.design: Tall capsule-shaped keeper made of pitch paint. Chalk white #F4F1E8 with one pale shade tone and a faint 3% dusty grain. Huge rounded mitten gloves. Two dot eyes #151A3D and short eyebrow dashes that carry every expression. No outlines, no mouth. He builds out of the goal line: the line lifts (trim path), folds and morphs into his body. At the end he sinks back into it. Each move gives off 8-12 chalk-dust particles. Poses: rise, ready, arms_crossed, reach_big, dive_left, dive_right, punch_clear, catch, rush_out, draw_wall, shuffle, lean_wrong, confused, squint, sink.
characters.role: The deadpan problem-setter. He never speaks and he learns after each goal. Chapter 1: he stands big in the middle. Chapter 2: he draws a chalk wall and guards the near post. Chapter 3: he punches the ball clear, then rushes out for the chip. Teaser: he cannot read the knuckleball at all.

characters.name: The Ball and its Line (motif)
characters.design: Orange ball #FF7A3D in every palette, with a darker crescent shade and a light rim on the lit edge. Tavi draws one chalk-white line around it in the cold open. The line is a true 3D great circle, projected every frame from the spin state, so every kind of spin reads on screen: slow backward roll (drive), sideways turn that is anticlockwise seen from above, with the front edge swinging left (curler), forward roll (volley), faster backward roll on a slow ball (chip), almost still (knuckleball). The ball squashes on contact. A ghost variant is a dashed outline at 40% with no line.
characters.role: The motif. Planted in the cold open ('Remember that line'), it shows the spin in every chapter. It pays off in the ending ('It told you everything') and in the teaser, where the line hardly turns.

characters.name: The Air Crowd
characters.design: Tiny round particles with two dot eyes, #7FB8FF in the X-ray palette and #F4FBFF in the Open Sky palette. They move in streams. Small #FF4FA3 puffs pop where they bump into each other. Faces show only in close-ups. In wide shots they are plain moving dashes.
characters.role: The metaphor for air. The crowd rushes past the ball, gets thrown aside by a spinning ball and shoves back. Used for sideways spin, the forward-spin dive, the chip float and the knuckleball flag.

scenes.narration: Nine at night. An empty pitch. <short pause> Just you, one ball, and a goalkeeper you made up. You call him Chalk. <short pause> You draw one line around the ball. Remember that line. <short pause> You shoot. <long pause> Over the bar. <short pause> You shout at it. It doesn't listen. <short pause> Chalk doesn't even move.
visual_beats: [1 s silent pre-roll] Dark sky #151A3D with a 3-layer star field. Four floodlights clunk on one after another. Each blooms 4 glow rings in 0.4 s.
'Nine at night.' Slow push (easeInOutSine, 8% over 5 s) past the stand. The stand clock shows nine.
'An empty pitch.' Wide side view in 4 parallax layers (0.2x, 0.5x, 1x, 1.3x). Dust drifts in the light beams. Behind the goal: a low fence and a dark car park.
'Just you, one ball,' Tavi walks in from the left and drops the ball 18 m out. Two small sim bounces, then it settles.
'and a goalkeeper you made up.' The goal-line paint peels up, folds and builds into Chalk (trim path 0.8 s, then morph). He blinks awake.
'You call him Chalk.' Chalk claps his mittens and a puff of chalk dust rises. Label 'CHALK' pops.
'You draw one line around the ball.' Top-down close-up: a marker draws one white line all the way round the orange ball (trim path, 30 frames).
'Remember that line.' The line glows once. Everything else dims by 20%.
'You shoot.' Side view. Three-step run-up with a long last stride. The standing foot lands behind the ball. Tavi's chest stays behind the ball (lean_back). Contact.
[long pause] The ball climbs on the MISS sim. In a tracking close-up the line rolls backward. The camera tilts up after it.
'Over the bar.' The ball clears the bar by about half a metre and drops over the fence into the car park. A faint car alarm chirps once.
'You shout at it.' Speech bubble from Tavi: 'DOWN! DOWN!' (snappy pop).
'It doesn't listen.' The car alarm chirps again. The bubble shrinks away.
'Chalk doesn't even move.' The camera eases back to Chalk: arms crossed, one eyebrow up, feet exactly where they were.
scenes.transition_out: Zoom-through: the camera rushes back to the spot and into Tavi's boot at the contact frame. The frame freezes and s02 opens on it.
facts_used: No narrated numbers. Bar height 2.44 m in the sim comes from 'A full-size goal is 7.32 m wide and 2.44 m high' (chip safe list).
'clears the bar by about half a metre' (visual) is sim geometry: ball centre about 3.06 m, ball bottom about 2.95 m, bar 2.44 m.
scenes.physics_sim: MISS: start 18 m out, central, z0 0.11 m. 21 m/s (76 km/h), 18 deg up, 0 deg sideways. Backspin 5 rev/s, spinAxis [0,-1,0] (top of the ball turning back toward the kicker). Cd 0.25, Cl from the kit model (about 0.20 at launch, lift about 1.9 N). Checks: ball centre about 3.06 m high at the goal line after about 1.05 s (ball bottom about 2.95 m, so it clears the bar by about 0.5 m). Peak about 3.1 m. Lands about 30 m from the kick (12 m past the goal line) after about 1.9 s. Put the car park at that spot and fire the alarm on the landing frame. Control check for s20: the same launch with no spin crosses at about 1.25 m, under the bar.
sfx: floodlight clunk x4 with a rising electrical hum

scenes.narration: What went wrong? <short pause> Your foot touches the ball for about a hundredth of a second. After that, it's on its own. So that tiny moment decides everything. <short pause> Three kicks tonight. One idea. Spin. How much. Which way. Or none at all. <short pause> By lights out, you'll score this shot.
visual_beats: 'What went wrong?' Rewind: the MISS sim plays backward. The ball drops out of the sky onto Tavi's boot.
'Your foot touches the ball for about a hundredth of a second.' Freeze at contact, the ball slightly squashed on the laces. HUD stopwatch (JetBrains Mono) creeps from 0.000 to 0.009 s.
'After that, it's on its own.' Unfreeze. A dotted tether between boot and ball snaps with a small spark.
'So that tiny moment decides everything.' A fan of faint orange ghost paths (30%) sprays out from the contact point: low, curling, dipping, floating.
'Three kicks tonight.' Three paths brighten. Small icons tag them: laces, inside of foot, volley.
'One idea. Spin.' A lime spin arrow draws around the ball and the line starts to turn.
'How much. Which way.' The arrow speeds up, then flips its axis through four states: slow back, sideways, forward, back (0.5 s each).
'Or none at all.' The arrow fades and the line almost stops. One beat of silence.
'By lights out, you'll score this shot.' The ghost fan fades. One dotted path (DRIVE_L preview) skims low into the bottom-left corner. A tiny floodlight icon in the frame corner blinks off once.
[2.5 s hold] The camera cranes up to top-down. The pitch markings slide into the title 'THREE SPINS AND A LINE' in chalk letters (Rubik 800) with an orange underline. Original title sting.
scenes.transition_out: The title letters slide back into pitch markings. The camera tilts down to the ball spot, where chalk writes chapter card 1 on the grass.
facts_used: 'about a hundredth of a second' <- 'Foot and ball touch for only about 9 thousandths of a second (9.1 ms at 1000 Hz, 9.12 ms at 4500 fps)' (drive) and 'In a real curve kick, the foot touches the ball for only about 10 thousandths of a second (9.6 to 12 ms, measured at 2500 frames per second)' (curler). 'About' holds for both.
Stopwatch stops at 0.009 s because the shot on screen is a laces kick (drive value, about 9 ms).
'tiny moment', not 'blink': a real blink is 10 to 40 times longer than the contact, and s14 uses the blink as the longer yardstick.
scenes.physics_sim: MISS samples in reverse. Ghost fan at 30%: DRIVE_R, CURLER, VOLLEY and CHIP, all redrawn from one contact point. Promise path: DRIVE_L samples, dotted.
sfx: soft shimmer as the ghost paths fan out
three light pops on the icons
spin whirr that changes pitch with each axis
soft blip as the floodlight icon blinks
original title sting, 2.5 s rising three-note figure

scenes.narration: Problem one: a shot Chalk can't reach. Low and hard. <short pause> Strange fact: after a clean strike, the ball can move faster than your foot. How?
visual_beats: [1 s card] Chalk writes '1 · THE DRIVE' on the grass, subtitle 'slow spin'. The card's ball line rolls slowly backward.
'Problem one: a shot Chalk can't reach.' Chalk stands tall in the goal with arms wide. A pale reach bubble covers the middle of the goal.
'Low and hard.' Two small target boxes glow in the bottom corners, outside the bubble.
'Strange fact:' Side view of Tavi at the ball. A chalk '!' pops.

'after a clean strike, the ball can move faster than your foot.' Slow-motion replay (tag 'SLOW MOTION'). HUD bars ride along: FOOT (teal) and BALL (orange). After contact the BALL bar passes the FOOT bar. No digits.
'How?' A big chalk question mark. Chalk peeks round the post and scratches his head. The camera starts its push toward the boot.
scenes.transition_out: Push into the boot. The boot turns see-through and the X-ray leg builds inside it (match morph, 1 s).
facts_used: No spoken number. 'faster than your foot' <- 'A skilled adult sends the ball about 1.35 times faster than the centre of the foot moves' and 'Strike quality rises with age: the ball/foot speed ratio goes from about 1.0 at U9 to 1.26 at U20.' The word 'can' covers younger players.
Subtitle 'slow spin' <- 'A normal laces drive spins about 4 turns per second' (the knuckleball, at about 0.9, is the one that almost stops).
scenes.physics_sim: Slow-motion replay: the first 0.25 s of DRIVE_R at 1/10 speed. The foot-speed bar reads from the rig.
sfx: soft pops on the target boxes
two rising whooshes for the bars

scenes.narration: First, the whip. The thigh swings, stops hard, and flings the shin. A skilled adult's knee moves at bike speed. The toes? Car speed, about eighty kilometres an hour. <short pause> Then, the trampoline. The ball squashes on your foot and springs back. Your leg is much heavier, so the ball can beat your foot.
visual_beats: 'First, the whip.' X-ray leg on the teal-ink grid (#06202A, grid #0F3A47). Bones glow #C9F6FF. Label 'WHIP' pops.

'The thigh swings, stops hard, and flings the shin.' At 1/20 speed the thigh glows pink #FF4FA3, swings, and stops as a small brake-pad icon clamps at the hip. A pulse of light runs down to the shin, which snaps forward. The leg morphs into a bullwhip for 0.8 s and back.
'A skilled adult's knee moves at bike speed.' Speed tag on the knee with a bicycle icon: '≈ 17 km/h'. Small note: 'skilled adult'.
'The toes? Car speed, about eighty kilometres an hour.' Speed tag on the toes with a car icon counts up to '≈ 80 km/h'.
'Then, the trampoline.' The ball turns into a cutaway with a small trampoline inside.
'The ball squashes on your foot and springs back.' The ball flattens a few centimetres against the laces. The mat stretches, then flings. A thin timer ring fills around the ball.

'Your leg is much heavier, so the ball can beat your foot.' Inset: a heavy trolley, about four times the ball's weight, bumps a ball, which leaves a little faster than the trolley. Back in X-ray, the ball leaves with a slightly longer arrow than the foot's arrow.
scenes.transition_out: Pan down the X-ray leg to the ankle. A divider draws in and splits the frame in two.
facts_used: 'bike speed' (knee) and 'about eighty kilometres an hour' (toes) <- 'At impact the toe area moves at about 22 m/s (79 km/h), but the knee moves at only about 5 m/s (17 km/h).' These are skilled-adult values, so the line says 'A skilled adult's knee'.
Squash (visual only) <- 'The ball squashes by about 3 to 7 cm, depending on how it is measured.'
Timer ring (visual only) <- 'Foot and ball touch for only about 9 thousandths of a second.'

'much heavier ... can beat your foot' plus the trampoline follow the drive mechanism correction: the ball beats the foot only because the effective striking mass (about 1.7-2.1 kg) is several times the ball's mass AND the ball springs back. 'can' covers young players (ratio about 1.0 at U9 to 1.26 at U20).
Trolley at about four times the ball (visual only) <- the same 1.7-2.1 kg against a 0.43 kg ball. A bowling ball (about 2600:1) would wrongly show almost twice the striker's speed.
sfx: low swoosh of the thigh, then a whip crack
trolley bump and a light ball tap

scenes.narration: A floppy ankle is a hammer with a loose head. It folds, and some of the hit leaks away. <short pause> So: toes down, ankle locked, middle of the laces. Hit near your toes, and the ball is about fifteen percent slower. Chalk gets there.
visual_beats: 'A floppy ankle is a hammer with a loose head.' Split screen with two X-ray ankles side by side. Left: the foot morphs into a hammer whose head hangs on a hinge.

'It folds, and some of the hit leaks away.' Left: at impact the toes are pushed further down and the hinge folds. A few orange leak puffs escape. The ball's arrow is only a little shorter than on the right.

'So: toes down, ankle locked, middle of the laces.' Right: the toes point down, a lock icon snaps onto the ankle, and foot and shin glow as one piece. A green band marks the middle of the laces. Three labels pop in order: TOES DOWN · ANKLE LOCKED · MIDDLE OF LACES.
'Hit near your toes, and the ball is about fifteen percent slower.' The contact dot slides to the toes. A speed bar drops, with the label '−15% (toe hit)'.

'Chalk gets there.' Floodlit inset: the slower TOE_HIT ball arrives low and late, and Chalk's diving mitten meets it. Saved. Then a ghost of the full-speed DRIVE_R slips past the same mitten into the net.
scenes.transition_out: Reverse zoom-through: pull back out of the boot to a side-on view of the pitch.
facts_used: 'about fifteen percent' <- 'The fastest spot is the middle of the laces, about 6 cm in front of the ankle joint. Contact at the toes or at the ankle gave about 15% less speed.'

Small loss on the loose-ankle side (no number spoken) <- 'In a kicking machine, a locked ankle gave about 4% more ball speed than a springy one.' The loose ankle folds toes-down, the direction given in the drive mechanism correction. The -15% label sits only on the toe-contact beat, so viewers do not mix the two.
scenes.physics_sim: Inset save: TOE_HIT = 18.4 m/s (66 km/h, 15% slower than DRIVE_R), 14 deg up, 8.5 deg right. Backspin 4 rev/s, spinAxis [-0.148,-0.989,0]. Cd 0.25. It crosses about 2.7 m right of centre, about 0.35 m high, after about 1.17 s (peak about 1.45 m). That is about 0.2 s after DRIVE_R, so Chalk's dive with the same reaction delay reaches it. The full-speed ghost is DRIVE_R (s07).

scenes.narration: Your foot swings like a playground swing, level only at the bottom. <short pause> So put your standing foot next to the ball. Put it behind, and your kicking foot is already rising. Hello, car park. <short pause> Knee and chest over the ball. Strike through the middle: speed, not spin. <short pause> The line turns slowly.
visual_beats: 'Your foot swings like a playground swing,' Side-on pitch view, Tavi at the ball. The swing arc draws from the hip and a small swing seat rides along it.
'level only at the bottom.' A chalk dot marks the low point. A flat arrow appears there.
'So put your standing foot next to the ball.' A flat disc marker lands next to the ball. A small arrow on the standing foot's toes points at the goal. The low point of the arc sits right at the ball.
'Put it behind, and your kicking foot is already rising.' The disc slides back and the low point moves back with it. The foot meets the ball on the way up (red arrow tilts up).
'Hello, car park.' A dotted ghost (the MISS path) clears the bar and drops over the fence onto a car roof. Hazard lights blink. It pays off the alarm from s01.
'Knee and chest over the ball.' The disc returns. Tavi's knee and chest move over the ball and the shin stands upright.
'Strike through the middle: speed, not spin.' A ring target on the ball, contact at the centre. An effort bar fills almost all SPEED with only a thin SPIN sliver.
'The line turns slowly.' Tracking close-up of DRIVE_R at 1/10 speed. The line rolls slowly backward. Label: 'slow spin'.
scenes.transition_out: The blinking hazard lights turn into the pop-in of the PracticeBoard (0.3 s swipe).

component_kit.name: FlightSim
component_kit.props: { name: string; v0:number; elevDeg:number; azimDeg:number; z0?:number; spinRps:number; spinAxis:[number,number,number]; cd:number; clFixed?:number; spinPush?: boolean; sideForce?: {peakN:number; wavelengthM:number; phase:number}; stopAt: 'goalLine'|'ground'|number; startFrame:number; slowMo?:number }
component_kit.notes: useFlight hook. Point mass 0.43 kg, radius 0.11 m, air 1.2 kg/m3, area 0.038 m2, gravity 9.81. Ball on the ground starts at z0 0.11 m. Air brake = 0.5*rho*A*Cd*v^2 against the velocity. Spin push = 0.5*rho*A*Cl*v^2 along unit(spinAxis x velocity), with Cl = min(0.35, 0.5*sqrt(r*omega/v)) unless clFixed is set. Spin decays 2%/s. sideForce (knuckle only) is a sine along the path. Integrate at dt 1/600 s and sample at 60 fps. Axis vectors, for a shot a degrees right of +x (heading (cos a, -sin a, 0)): backspin = -(sin a, cos a, 0), topspin = +(sin a, cos a, 0). Per shot: MISS, DRIVE_WALL, CHIP, CHIP_GHOST [0,-1,0]; DRIVE_R and TOE_HIT (a 8.5) [-0.148,-0.989,0]; DRIVE_L (a -8.5) [0.148,-0.989,0]; VOLLEY (a 10) [0.174,0.985,0]; CURLER (a 8) = 0.891 x [0,0,1] - 0.454 x (sin 8, cos 8, 0) = [-0.063,-0.450,0.891]; CURLER_AIM_MISS (a 0) [0,-0.454,0.891]. Named shots: MISS, DRIVE_R, DRIVE_L, DRIVE_WALL, TOE_HIT, CURLER, CURLER_AIM_MISS, DROP, VOLLEY, VOLLEY_GHOST, EASY, SMASH, BOUNCE_DRILL, CHIP, CHIP_GHOST, KNUCKLE (values in each scene; all checks were run again in this model). Precompute every shot to JSON in a build step. A validator checks each scene's stated values (height at the line within 0.1 m, side position within 0.1 m, time within 0.05 s). It also checks the signs: backspin pushes up, VOLLEY pushes down and CURLER pushes toward +y (left). So calculateMetadata never throws. The ball in flight moves on linear time with no design ease. Slow motion only when labelled.

music_cues: s01 cold open: a low original synth pad under the floodlight hum. One soft bell note on 'Remember that line'. Full silence on the miss. A small comic pluck on the car alarm and on 'Chalk doesn't even move'.

s02 title: the pad swells under the ghost fan. A small rising lift on 'By lights out, you'll score this shot.' Title sting: an original 2.5 s motif on a warm plucked synth and marimba, a rising three-note figure (one note per kick) that resolves on the title hold.

Ch1 (s03-s06): a steady low pulse at about 90-96 bpm, with a muted kick drum on each contact frame. In X-ray scenes, filter the music down and add a sub-drop into slow motion. A hard stop and a low comic blip on 'Hello, car park.'
Practice loop (s07, s12, s17, s18): one short, bright loop reused for every PracticeBoard, in the same key each time and ducked 12 dB, so viewers learn the 'use this' moment.
Ch2 (s08-s11): a floating major-key arpeggio whose pitch bends follow the curl, panned right to left with the ball. A soft granular 'crowd of air' texture in s10. A lift on the goal in s12.
Ch3 (s13-s16): a syncopated rhythm with a ticking hi-hat for timing tension. A short bass drop on 'It dives', then a brighter lift as the ball goes under the bar.
Chip mirror (s19-s20): the chapter 3 melody upside down on the left channel (chip) and the right way up on the right (volley). They merge into one chord as the halves join.
s21: a warm build to 'Low. Hard. In.', a beat of silence on 'No shouting needed', then four soft notes, one per ball in the spin row.
s22 knuckleball: a slightly detuned, wobbling synth over the practice-loop drums. It cuts to silence on 'Neither do you.', then the practice loop returns softly under 'Master the drive first.'
s23: the title motif returns slowly on piano and pad at the calmer pace. Silence under the last line, then one closing chord on the end card.
